BAGONG PILIPINAS Republic of the Philippines DEPARTMENT OF THE INTERIOR AND LOCAL GOVERNMENT DILG-NAPOLCOM Center, EDSA cor. Quezon Avenue, West Triangle, Quezon City SEP 162025 www.dilq.qov.ph NO. 117 s. 2025 JUDY ANN A. LAURENTE Proprietor/Operator Cha Gasoline Station Habag, Lanuza, Surigao del Sur Dear Ms. Laurente: This has reference to your letter dated 18 December 2024 requesting for reconsideration of legal opinion No. 87 s, 2024 issued by this Department, and appealing for due consideration based on investor welfare and good faith in relation to DAR Land Conversion Order you submitted for purposes of securing a business permit. You have provided several supporting documents, including the mayor's issued business permit, Department legal opinion, DAR endorsement, Confirmation/Certificate, Notice Order, building permit, and a Certificate of Non- Coverage, in the hope of reconsidering the legal position previously issued by this Department. At the outset, we emphasize that legal opinions rendered by this Department are advisory in nature. They are issued for guidance based on the facts and documents submitted and are not equivalent to judicial or quasi-judicial determinations. The Department is not vested with adjudicatory authority and cannot bind the parties in a manner similar to a court decision. Thus, aggrieved parties are always at liberty to seek recourse through the appropriate legal fora. Upon thorough re-evaluation of the relevant documents you submitted, we regret to inform you that no substantial legal or factual ground exists to warrant the amendment or modification of Legal Opinion No. 87, s. 2024. We qoute the salient part of this assailed opinion: "We opine that the DAR Conversion Order must not deviate from the LGU's Land Use Plan. The law is clear, the DAR shall refer to the comprehensive land use plan as the main reference regarding land use conversion applications". Verily, Legal Opinion No. 87, s. 2024, addressed a critical issue concerning compliance with national land use and land classification policies, particularly as it "Matino, Mahusay at Maaasahan" Trunkline No. (02) 8876 3454

relates to the conversion of agricultural land for commercial use. The core of the opinion rests on the regulatory hierarchy that binds local governments to national land use policies, as laid out in the Local Government Code (LGC) of 1991, particularly Sections 26, 27, and 447(a)(2), in relation to: 1. Section 20 of the LGC, which governs land reclassification by local government units (LGUs); and 2. The complementary authority of the Department of Agrarian Reform (DAR) over the conversion of agricultural lands pursuant to Republic Act No. 6657, or the Comprehensive Agrarian Reform Law of 1988. The opinion reiterates that local govemments cannot issue business permits for land uses that contravene national land classification or are inconsistent with comprehensive land use plans (CLUPs) unless duly converted through proper channels. While we recognize your assertion of good faith in relying on a DAR land conversion order, it must be emphasized that the burden of ensuring the sufficiency, validity, and accuracy of submitted documents lies with the applicant. Any deficiencies or misrepresentations—whether intentional or not—may be sufficient basis for an LGU to deny or revoke a business permit. Moreover, the Department must underscore the policy imperative of ensuring harmonization between national regulatory standards and local issuances. Legal Opinion No. 87, s. 2024, affirms this alignment. To allow LGUs to disregard potential violations of land conversion rules, even in the name of investor welfare, would undermine the integrity of the national-local regulatory framework, create inequity among similarly situated applicants, and may expose LGUs to legal liability for ultra vires acts. Finally, the principle of investor protection, while important, does not operate in a vacuum. It cannot supersede or excuse noncompliance with existing laws and regulations. Due diligence, including strict vetting of land use conversion documents, is essential for ensuring legal compliance and mitigating regulatory risk. In light of the foregoing, we find no compelling justification to revise or reverse Legal Opinion No. 87, s. 2024. The Department remains consistent in its legal interpretation that the issuance of business permits by local government units must strictly conform with national policies on land use, agrarian reform, and land conversion. Allowing exceptions outside the scope of existing regulations would not only undermine the legal framework established under the Local Government Code and related laws but also set a dangerous precedent that could compromise regulatory coherence and public accountability. Hence, the previous legal opinion stands, and no modification thereto is warranted at this time. Page 2 of 3

We hope to have assisted you on this matter. Very truly yours, BY AUTHORITY OF THE SECRETARY: . ROMEO P. BENITEZ A Undersecretary for External, Legal and Legislative Affairs OUSELLNRPB/LLLS-LRALLD/sbl/kbm Page 3 of 3
